# Reference 02 — FICTIONAL EP 3 456 789 B1, "Tyre valve with flexible elastomer seat"

**Publication number: FICTIONAL — this reference does not exist and is provided only to exercise the prior-art charting prompts.**

Proprietor (fictional): Vellmar Reifentechnik GmbH. Granted (fictional): 3 March 2021. Priority (fictional): 9 June 2018.

## Summary of disclosure

The reference concerns a tyre valve — for bicycles and light vehicles — in which the seat against which the poppet seals is an elastomeric ring (element 12) rather than a metal shoulder, "so that the seal is maintained despite particulate contamination of the sealing surfaces" (paragraph [0008]). The stated problem is sealing against dust and sealant particles; the reference does not describe removing deposits.

Paragraphs [0015]–[0021] and Fig. 2 describe the elastomer ring as an O-ring or a moulded lip seal of nitrile or fluoroelastomer, hardness 60–80 Shore A, retained in a groove in the valve body. Under inflation pressure the lip "deflects outward to enlarge the flow passage and reduce the pressure drop across the valve" (paragraph [0019]). On removal of the pump the lip "returns under its own elasticity" to seal (paragraph [0020]).

Paragraph [0024] notes that "the seat ring may alternatively be formed of a resilient thermoplastic elastomer or a spring steel lip seal" but gives no dimensions, geometry or further description of the spring steel variant.

Claim 1 (fictional) recites: a tyre valve comprising a body, a poppet, and a seat formed by an elastomeric ring retained in the body, the ring being deflectable outward by inflation pressure to enlarge the flow passage.

Dependent claim 4 (fictional) recites the seat being a lip seal deflectable by the poppet during opening.

## What is absent or ambiguous (reviewer's note for testing)

- The seat deflects under pressure, but the deflection enlarges the main flow passage; there is no separate purge gap, no over-travel distinct from normal opening, and no two-stage spring.
- No shape-memory or superelastic alloy. The "spring steel lip seal" in [0024] is the closest passage and should be charted carefully: it is a single sentence with no structure described.
- No wiping or self-cleaning function is described; the elastomer is chosen to seal around particles, which is the opposite mechanism.
- Nothing is said about sealant swelling the elastomer, though nitrile in latex/ammonia sealant is known to swell — this is a point the differentiation matrix could use only if the disclosure supports it.
